# One-Day Meal Plan for Marathon Training Athlete

Here is a one-day meal plan for an athlete training for a marathon with high carbohydrate loading needs:

* **Calorie Target:** Approximately 3,500 calories
* **Macronutrient Breakdown:** Protein (105g / 12%), Carbs (525g / 60%), Fat (117g / 30%)

## Meal Plan:

* **Breakfast (6:30 AM):** Oatmeal (100g dry weight) with banana (150g), honey (30g), and sunflower seeds (20g). Whole milk (250ml).
    * Protein: 18g, Fat: 12g, Carbs: 95g

* **Mid-Morning Snack (9:00 AM):** Whole wheat bagel (85g) with jam (25g) and peanut butter (20g). Orange juice (250ml).
    * Protein: 12g, Fat: 9g, Carbs: 72g

* **Lunch (12:30 PM):** Grilled lean chicken breast (150g) with white rice (120g cooked) and steamed carrots (150g). Olive oil (10ml).
    * Protein: 42g, Fat: 12g, Carbs: 85g

* **Pre-Training Snack (3:00 PM):** Rice cakes (50g) with honey (25g) and raisins (40g). Sports drink (500ml, 6% carbs).
    * Protein: 6g, Fat: 2g, Carbs: 110g

* **Dinner (7:00 PM):** Baked lean ground turkey (160g) with sweet potato (200g) and steamed green beans (180g). Olive oil (10ml).
    * Protein: 38g, Fat: 15g, Carbs: 75g

* **Evening Snack (9:30 PM):** Pasta (80g dry weight) with marinara sauce (100g) and lean ground beef (80g).
    * Protein: 22g, Fat: 12g, Carbs: 68g

* **Before Bed (10:30 PM):** Low-fat Greek yogurt (200g) with honey (15g) and seeds (15g).
    * Protein: 20g, Fat: 3g, Carbs: 35g

---

**Notes:** This meal plan emphasizes carbohydrate-rich whole grains, lean proteins, and plenty of fruits/vegetables to fuel marathon training. All foods are nut-free to accommodate the severe allergy. Timing includes pre- and post-training nutrition to optimize endurance performance.

# One-Day Meal Plan for Vegetarian Athlete - Muscle Gain & Strength Focus

**Athlete Profile:** 180 cm, 85 kg, Heavy Lifting Training Cycle

* **Calorie Target:** Approximately 3,100 calories
* **Macronutrient Breakdown:** Protein (165g), Fat (95g), Carbs (380g)

---

## **Meal Plan:**

* **Breakfast (7:00 AM):** Greek yogurt (250g, plain) with granola (60g), sliced banana (120g), and ground flaxseed (15g). Whole wheat toast (50g) with almond butter (20g).
  * Protein: 28g, Fat: 18g, Carbs: 75g

* **Mid-Morning Snack (10:00 AM):** Protein smoothie made with plant-based protein powder (30g), oat milk (240g), peanut butter (25g), and blueberries (100g).
  * Protein: 30g, Fat: 15g, Carbs: 45g

* **Lunch (1:00 PM):** Chickpea and quinoa Buddha bowl with mixed greens (150g), roasted chickpeas (150g), cooked quinoa (100g dry weight), sweet potato (150g), cucumber (50g), and tahini dressing (20g). Side of whole grain crackers (40g).
  * Protein: 22g, Fat: 18g, Carbs: 95g

* **Pre-Workout Snack (4:00 PM):** Whole wheat bagel (80g) with hummus (40g) and sliced tomato (50g). Orange (150g).
  * Protein: 12g, Fat: 8g, Carbs: 85g

* **Dinner (7:30 PM):** Lentil and vegetable stir-fry with cooked red lentils (150g cooked), broccoli (200g), bell peppers (100g), mushrooms (100g), brown rice (120g cooked), and sesame oil (15g). Tofu cubes (120g) included.
  * Protein: 40g, Fat: 20g, Carbs: 65g

* **Evening Snack (9:30 PM):** Cottage cheese (150g, low-fat) with walnuts (20g) and hemp seeds (10g).
  * Protein: 33g, Fat: 16g, Carbs: 15g

---

**Nutritional Notes:** This meal plan emphasizes plant-based protein sources (legumes, tofu, Greek yogurt, nuts, seeds) to support muscle hypertrophy during heavy lifting. The timing around workouts ensures adequate carbohydrates and calories for recovery and performance. All foods are vegetarian-friendly and nutrient-dense.
